items.title: Walter Booker and Jimmy Cobb interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995
items.q: The interviewee narrates historical facts about Count Basie's band and Joe Williams, stating 'when he was with Count Basie’s band' and 'I remember seeing Duke Ellington’s band and the Count Basie band', but does not describe a personal interaction or relationship with Count Basie himself.

ctx.x: How do you feel like his sound typifies jazz vocals?

Oh well he did, you know he did a lot to bring a certain type of blues to certain people. You know because when he was with Count Basie’s band he matter-of-factly kind of saved Count Basie’s band for many. Because at that time the bands weren’t doing that well. So they got Joe and Joe was a real favorite singer, so he kind of helped the band. He helped them so much that I think Basie started to call him his son. So Joe kind of educated people to that music, you know, people that probably wasn’t listening to it…
Absolutely. That’s probably what happened, yeah, he did raise up the, he did widen the listening audience’s ears to the blues form, and acceptance of it, you know what I mean?
